title: Mahajanapadas
capsule: The Mahajanapadas (Sanskrit: 'great realm-footholds') were sixteen major kingdoms and oligarchic republics that dominated the Indian subcontinent roughly from 600 to 350 BCE, as catalogued in Buddhist and Jain texts including the Anguttara Nikaya. The list includes monarchies such as Magadha, Kosala, Avanti, and Vatsa, as well as republican confederacies (ganas) such as the Vajjian confederacy centered on Vaishali. Magadha progressively absorbed its rivals under the Haryanka, Shishunaga, and Nanda dynasties, creating the territorial base that Chandragupta Maurya unified into the Maurya Empire around 322 BCE. The era was also the milieu in which Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) and Mahavira preached, and in which the earliest Indian urban centers flourished.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extents of individual Mahajanapadas are inferred from Pali and Sanskrit textual geography and limited archaeology; boundaries between kingdoms were fluid and poorly defined compared to later administrative empires.
